title: Compare within one text first
statement: Before asking students to compare two texts, give them a single text that makes the comparison itself.
detail: A curriculum map describes a compare-contrast text on birds and reptiles as a scaffolded within-text comparison that builds toward cross-text comparison later, and tags another lesson, in which students write their own comparison of four civilisations they have read about, as cross-text comparison (`downloads/_G3 curriculum Map.xlsx - Curric Map.csv`). This is a sequencing choice in one map; no outcome was measured.

evidence.quote: A scaffolded within-text comparison to build skills toward cross-text comparison later.
A reader needs a bounded account of each source's main ideas before combining contributions without blending them.
Teach COMPARE here first, so the only new load is the compare move.
